prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2017 manifesto sets out a plan to rebuild a fairer Britain that works for the many, not the few. It answers falling living standards, insecure work and overstretched public services with investment, stronger rights, and democratic control over key services—alongside a jobs‑first Brexit.

Economy and tax
- Upgrade the economy via a £250bn National Transformation Fund and a National Investment Bank with regional development banks, focused on high-skill, low‑carbon growth and balanced regional development.
- Industrial missions: 60% zero‑carbon/renewable energy by 2030; 3% of GDP on R&D.
- Fair taxation: no rises in income tax for 95% (those under £80k), no VAT or personal NIC rises; top 5% and large corporations pay more; clamp down on avoidance; protect small business with lower rates and action on late payments.
- Fiscal Credibility Rule: eliminate day‑to‑day deficit within five years while investing for growth.

Ownership and finance
- Widen economic democracy: double the co‑operative sector; a “right to own” for employees on business sales; insource public services.
- Bring rail, mail, water and energy networks into public ownership to cut bills and raise accountability; cap energy prices during transition; mass home insulation; ban fracking.
- Reform finance: strong ring‑fence, diverse local banking, protect communities from branch closures.

Brexit and trade
- Accept the referendum; secure a close new EU partnership that prioritises jobs, standards and the benefits of the Single Market/Customs Union; guarantee EU nationals’ rights; reject “no deal”; maintain cooperation on research, security and energy.
- Pro‑trade with high standards, transparency, SME support and human‑rights clauses.

Work, rights and pay
- 20‑point plan: £10 Living Wage by 2020; end zero‑hours; equal rights from day one; repeal Trade Union Act and expand sectoral bargaining; abolish tribunal fees; 20:1 pay ratios in public sector/procurement; stronger protections against discrimination and unfair redundancy; crack down on bogus self‑employment.

Education
- National Education Service, free at the point of use, from early years to adult learning.
- Expand affordable childcare, restore Sure Start; reverse school cuts, cut class sizes, free primary meals.
- Free FE and ESOL; restore EMA; improve apprenticeships.
- Abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants.

Health and care
- Over £30bn extra for the NHS; end pay cap; safe staffing; reverse privatisation; free hospital parking; faster access to care.
- Ring‑fence mental health; end out‑of‑area placements; school counselling.
- Build a National Care Service; £8bn social care boost and long‑term funding reform.

Homes and communities
- Over 1m new homes; at least 100k social homes a year; suspend Right to Buy where not replaced; end bedroom tax.
- Three‑year tenancies, cap rent rises, ban letting fees; plan to end rough sleeping.
- 10,000 more police; stronger action on violence against women and girls; restore legal aid access; rebuild fire, prison and probation services.

Infrastructure, transport and environment
- HS2 to Scotland, Crossrail 2, nationwide rail electrification; bring rail into public ownership; empower municipal buses; universal superfast broadband and 5G.
- Clean Air Act; protect habitats and forests; cut plastic waste; plant 1m trees; uphold animal welfare and hunting bans.

Equality, democracy and the world
- Strengthen the EHRC; gender‑audit policy; advance LGBT and disability rights; tackle racism and hate crime; votes at 16; Lords reform; deeper devolution.
- Defence: spend at least 2% of GDP; renew Trident; modernise capabilities.
- Foreign policy rooted in human rights and international law; suspend arms sales where IHL is at risk; recognise Palestine; uphold 0.7% aid, fight tax havens.

This is a fully costed programme to share prosperity, restore public services and put dignity, security and opportunity at the heart of national life.
</text>
